page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.large is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 7T83 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz, delivering 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with 2 threads. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and FMA.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile characterized by strong single-core CPU capabilities but limited multi-core and memory performance. In stress-ng single-core CPU tests, the instance scored 2685.48, placing it in the top 25% of tested hardware. However, its multi-core CPU performance of 2691.38 falls into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only small block cached memory bandwidth measured at 126.98 GB/sec and uncached large block write bandwidth at 16.11 GB/sec. Similarly, database operations and Redis SET operations scored in the bottom 10%, reflecting the memory and multi-core constraints.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-core performance, the ecs.c7a.large offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require consistent single-threaded execution without massive memory footprints. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio positions it as a compute-optimized entry-level instance. It is best suited for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, text processing, and small-scale software compilation. It is less appropriate for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded high-performance computing, or large-scale parallel processing due to its low memory bandwidth and multi-core limitations.
